cover.title:
Investment
Theses
cover.subtitle: How we map each sector, where we are searching, and what has to be true for us to write a cheque.

divider.name: Artificial Intelligence
divider.subtitle: Data, regulation, physical access and talent decide the rest.

map.eyebrow: Artificial Intelligence · How we see the AI stack · September 2026
map.title: Capital decides most layers of AI. We fund `the layers it does not`.
map.subtitle: Data, regulation, physical access and talent decide the rest.

rows.decides: Developer adoption decides this, and Indian teams compete globally.
Training environments decide it, and Indian factories and roads are closed.
Indian law creates this market. Labelling and take-down rules took effect in February 2026.

others.text: Kroop AI, Repello AI, Enkrypt AI

rows.detail: indic, speech and on-device, not frontier
rows.decides: Capital decides frontier models. Data decides Indic and speech.

rows.detail: industry models and small language models
rows.decides: The company trains the model on its own data. Workflow on a rented model is not this.
The science is proven and Indian platforms are underfunded against it.
Capex decides it. Sovereign cloud and serving efficiency are the exceptions.
Many companies, little technological differentiation. Distribution is the moat.

footers.label: The export engine
footers.text: 2,117 GCCs, 2.4 million people, and more than 1,200 running AI mandates.

footers.label: The domestic engine
footers.text: RBI has required payment data to sit in India since 2018. The 2026 IT Rules add labelling and take-down duties.

tests.eyebrow: Artificial Intelligence · What wins here, and why now · September 2026
tests.title: Three things `stay valuable` when models get cheaper
tests.subtitle: General models are rented. Domain data, design quality and regulation are not.
tests.testsLabel: What makes a company defensible here

tests.title: A dataset that takes years to assemble
tests.body: Twenty-two languages of telephony audio. Factory floors, Indian roads, defence trials. Collected over years. The collection is the asset.
tests.evidence: $234M — raised by Sarvam in 2026, on an Indic data asset.

tests.title: Adoption, not spend
tests.body: Developer adoption decides these layers. A tool wins on how good it is, and Indian teams compete globally on that.
tests.evidence: Palo Alto Networks bought Portkey, an India-founded gateway, in 2026.

tests.title: A position foreign vendors cannot occupy
tests.body: When the rule names the jurisdiction, the foreign vendor is excluded before evaluation. Two-hour takedowns became law in February.
tests.evidence: 5M — Indian users, the threshold above which platforms must run automated detection since February 2026.

whyNow.label: Cost ↓
whyNow.body: Compute is no longer what stops an Indian team from starting.
whyNow.source: IndiaAI compute pillar, subsidised at ₹65-92 per GPU hour

whyNow.label: Demand ↑
whyNow.body: Compliance now has a fixed date.
whyNow.source: DPDP obligations commence, with penalties up to ₹250 crore

whyNow.label: Supply ↑
whyNow.body: Four times the same period in 2025.
whyNow.source: raised by Indian AI startups across 57 deals (Inc42) in the first half of 2026

tests.notFund: Frontier model training runs. Orchestration a hyperscaler gives away free. Copilots built on rented models, where distribution is the moat.
tests.changeView: Frontier models closing the Indic gap. Hyperscalers certified for regulated workloads. Subsidised compute still unused in 2027.

divider.name: Aerospace and Surveillance
divider.subtitle: Indian demand gets these companies started. A globally competitive part is what makes them worth owning.

map.eyebrow: Aerospace and Surveillance · How we see the sector · September 2026
map.title: We fund `the parts inside the platform`, not the platform.
map.subtitle: Indian demand gets these companies started. A globally competitive part is what makes them worth owning.

rows.detail: GPS-denied navigation, flight computers, secure comms
rows.decides: A qualified part is sole-sourced for the platform's life.
Trials history. Every other bidder imports the same detector.

rows.detail: imagery missions, geospatial analytics, coastal radar
rows.decides: The archive compounds while the satellite depreciates. Only Indian firms may own the data.
The prime cannot build the engine, and cannot change it once it flies.
The approvals, not the machines. A qualified process transfers to nobody.
Anyone can assemble a drone. Few hold the survey data or the certifications.

rows.detail: heavy checks, engine shops, ammunition, armour
rows.decides: Capacity and price decide it, not technology.

footers.label: Global supply chain
footers.text: Airbus takes India sourcing to $2 billion before 2030, building A320, A330 and A350 parts at Aequs, Dynamatic, Gardner and Mahindra.

footers.label: Listing route
footers.text: Seven Indian aerospace and defence suppliers have listed since 2021, among them MTAR, Data Patterns, Azad Engineering and Aequs.

tests.eyebrow: Aerospace and Surveillance · What wins here, and why now · September 2026
tests.title: A qualified part is bought `for the life of the platform`.
tests.subtitle: Three things get a company qualified in the first place.
tests.testsLabel: What makes a company defensible here

tests.title: Qualification locks the supplier in
tests.body: Once qualified onto a platform, a part stays for its life. The barrier is time, not capital.
tests.evidence: 10,000 — inertial systems Aeron Systems has in service with HAL, BEL, DRDO and the Navy.

tests.title: What cannot be imported is reserved
tests.body: Fine-resolution mapping and GPS-denied navigation are closed to foreign suppliers by regulation.
tests.evidence: ₹25 CR — the contract QuBeats won to build navigation that works without GPS.

tests.title: The work accumulates and keeps selling
tests.body: Every survey flown and every threat library built is an asset a competitor cannot buy.
tests.evidence: 45,000 — villages Aereo has mapped, an archive no competitor can buy.

whyNow.label: Exports ↑
whyNow.body: Up 63% in a year. FY29 target: ₹50,000 crore.
whyNow.source: Ministry of Defence, defence exports FY2025-26

whyNow.label: Denial ↑
whyNow.body: GNSS interference, most over Amritsar and Jammu.
whyNow.source: Airports Authority of India to ICAO, Feb 2024 to Feb 2025

whyNow.label: Mandate →
whyNow.body: Only village land is surveyed at this accuracy. Not cities, farmland or infrastructure.
whyNow.source: National Geospatial Policy, Dec 2022

tests.notFund: Maintenance, structures and munitions, where a licensed plant and volume price decide it. Platforms already funded past our cheque size.
tests.changeView: Drone flights beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) still uncertified after 2026. An eVTOL certified outside of China. IRSA opens conformance testing to private vendors.

divider.name: Life Sciences
divider.subtitle: A company qualifies when it owns the IP and the clearance, holds data or a channel that cannot be assembled elsewhere, and can reach its next clearance or clinical readout inside the round we lead.

map.eyebrow: Life Sciences · Where we invest · September 2026
map.title: Indian companies now originate diagnostics, devices and therapies, and `hold the clearances` behind them.
map.subtitle: A company qualifies when it owns the IP and the clearance, holds data or a channel that cannot be assembled elsewhere, and can reach its next clearance or clinical readout inside the round we lead.

rows.decides: Ownership of both instrument and consumable, and inclusion in public testing protocols.
CDSCO Class C clearance, then repeat purchase after the first pilot. Both depend on the ability to work with hospitals.

rows.detail: implants, neuro devices, monitors, drug delivery
rows.decides: Domestic design at roughly a tenth of import price, cleared to the same device class.
Interpretation against Indian population data; sequencing itself is commoditised.
Equity in the platform output rather than fee-for-service analysis revenue.
Grant capital funds the asset to clinic, so the first equity round enters de-risked.
Preclinical data packages built at Indian cost, then a CDSCO trial pathway run domestically.
Qualification into validated production lines, which are re-specified about once a decade.

rows.detail: care platforms, health IT, generic formulations
rows.decides: Distribution, price or a manufacturing scale a global incumbent already holds.

footers.label: The industrial base
footers.text: A ₹17.4 lakh crore bioeconomy, 4.8% of GDP, on vaccines, generics and CRO capacity. Programmes run at a fifth to a tenth of US cost against the same ISO 13485 and CDSCO standards.

footers.label: The data base
footers.text: GenomeIndia has released 10,000 whole genomes, an input Indian interpretation companies did not have three years ago.

tests.eyebrow: Life Sciences · What we look for, and why now · September 2026
tests.title: Three conditions shape how we look at a life sciences company
tests.subtitle: We require all three.

tests.title: The IP and the clearance are owned
tests.body: The patents sit with the company, and the approval or protocol listing built on them takes years to earn and stays with whoever earned it. We do not underwrite licensed-in science or distribution of someone else's clearance.
tests.evidence: ImmunoACT holds CDSCO authorisation for India's first approved CAR-T. Molbio's Truenat is one of two rapid molecular TB tests the WHO has endorsed. Peptris holds a US FDA orphan drug designation.

tests.title: Data that cannot be assembled elsewhere
tests.body: Sequencing, compute and cloud are commodities. Interpretation against Indian population data is not.
tests.evidence: 10,000 — whole genomes GenomeIndia has released; 4baseCare holds one of the largest genomic and clinical collections apart from MSKCC.

tests.title: The next milestone is achievable
tests.body: The clearance or clinical readout that re-rates the company must be achievable within realistic timelines. At Indian cost most are, and grant capital extends the runway further.
tests.evidence: 60,000 — patients Alfaleus tested on 350+ shipped devices before raising ₹3.5 crore; ImmunoACT ran its pivotal trial to approval at Indian cost.

whyNow.label: Market ↑
whyNow.body: The demand is already funded, by hospital and government budgets rather than by venture capital.
whyNow.source: of India's medical device consumption, FY24; imports near ₹63,000 crore

whyNow.label: Capital ↑
whyNow.body: Loans at 3-4% over 12-15 years, or equity to 25%, for TRL 4-6 companies. Live since May 2026.
whyNow.source: allocated to BIRAC as an RDI fund manager

whyNow.label: Exit ↑
whyNow.body: Institutional subscription reached 186.39 times; listed at ₹980 against a ₹807 issue price.
whyNow.source: Molbio's IPO, listed 17 August 2026

tests.notFund: Care delivery businesses. Licensed-in IP with no owned patents. Services revenue reported as platform revenue.
tests.changeView: Clearance timelines or trial costs pushing the next milestone beyond one round. A foreign vendor clearing CDSCO faster than a domestic one.

divider.name: Robotics
divider.subtitle: The demand gap is real, and most of it will be filled by assembled systems with no defensible layer.

map.eyebrow: Robotics · How we see the robotics map · September 2026
map.title: Most robotics companies are integrators. We fund the ones that `own a layer`.
map.subtitle: The demand gap is real, and most of it will be filled by assembled systems with no defensible layer.

rows.decides: Indian warehouses are narrower, less structured and more cost-sensitive than these systems were designed for.

rows.detail: task specific robots, manipulation policy, robot learning
rows.decides: A machine that is as complex as the task demands, and no more. The policy shops inside a machine the company owns.
The arm is a commodity. Value sits in the software and the hands that do high-mix work without reprogramming.
Municipal and plant procurement is a qualification gate, and no imported system is tuned for Indian field conditions.
Regulatory clearance, then hospital go-to-market. Both take years and neither is a technology problem.

rows.detail: actuators, reducers, force and tactile sensors
rows.decides: Scale sits with Japanese, German and Chinese suppliers. An Indian component wins only bundled into a system that needs it.
Sea trials build a real moat, but the government is the only buyer and there is no visible order book yet.
Capital, and a first industrial customer. Consumer and assistive robots are possible for us, but not where we look first.
The same problem everywhere, so there is no Indian advantage to build on.

footers.label: The factory engine
footers.text: India's entire installed base is ~50,000 industrial robots, tenth in the world. There is almost nothing here to displace.

footers.label: The outcome engine
footers.text: GreyOrange has raised over $110 million and Reliance-backed Addverb is raising over $100 million to expand. Indian warehouse robotics already produces companies at scale.

tests.eyebrow: Robotics · What wins here, and why now · September 2026
tests.title: The assembled robot `is not the moat`. Three other things are.
tests.subtitle: Every part of a robot is purchasable. Three things are not.
tests.testsLabel: What makes a robotics company durable

tests.title: The Indian environment is a potential moat
tests.body: Indian manufacturing is starting to automate from a low base and is at an inflection point. Its factories and warehouses differ from those abroad and adapting to them takes years on site.
tests.evidence: $28M — 2026's largest Indian robot round, raised by Unbox Robotics (built for Indian parcel floors) in January.

tests.title: A qualification gate the foreign vendor cannot pass
tests.body: Naval sea trials, hospital procurement, refinery certification, municipal contracts. Passing takes years, and the buyer's rules often exclude the foreign vendor.
tests.evidence: Genrobotics sells into a statutory ban on manual sewer cleaning, with a central scheme subsidising the replacements.

tests.title: Own one layer, sell the system around it
tests.body: Chassis, motors, gearboxes, even the policy models are purchasable, and a bare Indian component cannot match Japanese or Chinese scale.
tests.evidence: Perceptyne builds its own actuators, sensing and policy, and sells the cell.

whyNow.label: Installed ↑
whyNow.body: A record year, and sixth in the world ahead of every European market except Germany.
whyNow.source: IFR World Robotics 2025, India installations for 2024

whyNow.label: Capital ↑
whyNow.body: Raised by Indian companies building robots in seven months, already past all of 2025.
whyNow.source: Venture Intelligence via Entrackr, January to July 2026

whyNow.label: Cost ↓
whyNow.body: The bought-in stack gets cheaper every year.
whyNow.source: Unitree R1 humanoid, launched July 2025 at 39,900 yuan

tests.notFund: Integration sold as robotics. Demos that have never run a full shift. Robots with no route to market. Egocentric data capture sold as robotics.
tests.changeView: A manipulation model that removes years on site. A foreign vendor clearing a gate built to exclude it. An Indian conglomerate running a humanoid programme with paying industrial customers.

divider.name: Fabless Semiconductor
divider.subtitle: We fund companies that already have line of sight on a customer.

map.eyebrow: Fabless Semiconductor · How we see the stack · September 2026
map.title: Design capability is not the constraint for strong Indian teams. `Finding the customer` is.
map.subtitle: We fund companies that already have line of sight on a customer.

rows.decides: Whether a chip company anywhere will pay for the tool.

rows.detail: inference, edge AI, RISC-V cores, MCUs
rows.decides: Turning one tape-out into repeat commercial orders.
A small team that has taped out before.
A buyer who places a second order.

others.text: FermionIC, WiSig, XARK Tech, Mbit Wireless

rows.decides: A defence programme that pays for the qualification cycle.

rows.detail: secure elements, root of trust, PUFs
rows.decides: Certification, then a place in a procurement specification.
The process makes the sensor, so there is little to design.
Hundreds of millions per generation, and the CPU IP is closed.

footers.label: The state engine
footers.text: ISM 2.0 and the Design Linked Incentive (DLI) provide grants to smaller companies and equity to larger ones.

footers.label: The acquirer engine
footers.text: Global chip companies have acquired Indian design IP in four transactions since 2024.

tests.eyebrow: Fabless Semiconductor · What wins here, and why now · September 2026
tests.title: Indian fabless companies now have `two routes to an exit`
tests.subtitle: Global buyers acquire companies with competitive IP. Domestic demand can carry a company to listing.
tests.testsLabel: What makes a company defensible here

tests.title: IP that is hard to reproduce
tests.body: A small team that has shipped silicon produces IP an incumbent cannot scale quickly. Globally competitive from day 1, especially in RF and analog.
tests.evidence: Infineon agreed to buy C2i in August 2026 for its datacenter power IP.

tests.title: India as the proving ground
tests.body: Companies win their first customers and repeat orders in India. The product matures at home before it competes abroad.
tests.evidence: May 2026 — when Mindgrove declared its RISC-V microcontroller ready for mass production.

tests.title: Licensable IP, sold on standards
tests.body: Licensable cores and design tools sell on quality and standard positions. One good block ships inside many customers' chips.
tests.evidence: 50+ — silicon-proven IP blocks Terminus Circuits licenses; partnered with SiFive in April 2026.

whyNow.label: Cost ↓
whyNow.body: A team can start a processor without a license negotiation.
whyNow.source: RISC-V is an open instruction set

whyNow.label: Exits ↑
whyNow.body: Strategic buyers now pay for Indian IP.
whyNow.source: Infineon agreed to acquire C2i Semiconductors, a Yali holding

whyNow.label: Supply ↑
whyNow.body: The Indian fabless cohort is now large enough to source from and we have a large talent pool from GCCs.
whyNow.source: sanctioned under the Design Linked Incentive scheme

tests.notFund: Fabs and packaging. Frontier digital SoCs. Design services billed by the hour.
tests.changeView: An Indian security block licensed to a third party. A merchant foundry offering a qualified MEMS process. No DLI company past ₹100 crore by 2028.

divider.name: Smart Manufacturing
divider.subtitle: A regulator, an auditor or a customer's inspection is usually the reason to buy, and the reason to switch supplier.

map.eyebrow: Smart Manufacturing · How we see the Indian factory · September 2026
map.title: In Indian manufacturing, `qualification decides who wins`.
map.subtitle: A regulator, an auditor or a customer's inspection is usually the reason to buy, and the reason to switch supplier.

rows.decides: Vendor accuracy converges. The cost of each new line stays high.

rows.detail: legacy machine connectivity, MES, batch records, traceability
rows.decides: Most plants still run old machines and paper records. The first system that connects is rarely replaced.
Plants buy repeatability and local service. Assembly is copied.
A cheaper, cleaner way to make a known product. Switching suppliers means requalifying, rarely happens.
Most of this layer assembles gateways. Few own the sensing.
The technology travels. The buyer is a farmer, not a plant.
Project work, priced site by site. The next one costs the same.

footers.label: Who is forcing the purchase
footers.text: Three compliance deadlines passed by January 2026. Plants are now inspected against all three.

footers.label: Who is building new capacity
footers.text: ₹69,548 crore of new electronics factories approved since April 2025. Systems are being chosen now.

tests.eyebrow: Smart Manufacturing · What wins here, and why now · September 2026
tests.title: The technology is rarely the hard part. `Qualifying it in a plant` is.
tests.subtitle: Three things here are hard to copy. None of them is the technology.
tests.testsLabel: What makes a company hard to replace

tests.title: Software alone does not get onto the production line
tests.body: Plants are offline and budgets are written for equipment. Everything that works on the line ships hardware.
tests.evidence: SwitchOn runs its models on the line. Folium Sensing builds its own reader.

tests.title: The first system validated, or supplier qualified, stays
tests.body: Switching a validated system, or a qualified supplier, means repeating the audit. Getting in now is cheap; it will not stay cheap.
tests.evidence: 400+ — regulated plants Leucine has reached from zero since 2019, against incumbents dating to 2001.

tests.title: The winner installs fastest, not most accurately
tests.body: Accuracy gaps close within a year or two. The cost of validating one more line does not, and that is where the margin sits.
tests.evidence: $8M — raised by SwitchOn in July 2026, which runs 170 lines across 60+ plants.

whyNow.label: Rules ↑
whyNow.body: The December 2025 deadline was not extended. Only 1,700 of 8,500 plants applied.
whyNow.source: Revised Schedule M; inspections from Jan 2026

whyNow.label: Imports ↓
whyNow.body: India plans to stop importing SCADA for the grid. No domestic supplier base exists.
whyNow.source: Central Electricity Authority plan, Aug 2026

whyNow.label: Capital ↑
whyNow.body: A generalist fund led a $10M Series A into Fabheads. The median cheque is $3M.
whyNow.source: nearly 30 rounds across CY2025 and CY2026

tests.notFund: Businesses that scale on working capital. Machines assembled in India with everything imported. Compliance software no plant has installed.
tests.changeView: Schedule M enforcement relaxed. An Indian industrial group buying a factory-AI company. A foreign vendor winning the first-time plants.

divider.name: Other Deep Tech
divider.subtitle: In all four, the Indian buyer has only just appeared. We seek out the startups that supply them.

otherDeepTech.eyebrow: Other deep tech · Where we play · September 2026
otherDeepTech.title: Four more sectors where Yali invests selectively

rows.decides: Selling components to launch and satellite companies, in India and abroad.

others.text: Bellatrix, Manastu Space, InspeCity, AADYAH Aerospace

rows.decides: The first government order. Key distribution is already won; sensing is still open.
A product that earns revenue without building a factory and without selling to a utility.
Getting approved as a supplier, by plants that are choosing their suppliers right now.

otherDeepTech.subtitle: In all four, the Indian buyer has only just appeared. We seek out the startups that supply them.

notInvesting.segment: Cells and gigafactories, green hydrogen systems, quantum computers, whole launch vehicles, charging networks
notInvesting.decides: The first unit costs more than we invest in a company, or the only buyer is the government.

footers.label: What changed
footers.text: Export controls and new national missions created a domestic buyer in all four sectors at once.

footers.label: What did not
footers.text: Demand is new. So the first suppliers to qualify will hold their positions for years.

tests.eyebrow: Other Deep Tech · What we look for, and why now · September 2026
tests.title: Three tests decide where we invest in these sectors
tests.subtitle: The same three tests apply in all four sectors. They rule out more companies than they let in.

tests.title: The buyer is named and already switching
tests.body: An Indian company needs this input to ship its own product, and is willing to buy it from a young startup.
tests.evidence: Dreamfly sells drone packs to Tata Advanced Systems and L&T.

tests.title: The qualification is still open
tests.body: Once a supplier is approved into a product specification, it stays there for years. We want the places where no one has won that spot yet.
tests.evidence: No approved semiconductor plant in India has qualified a domestic materials supplier.

tests.title: The first commercial unit fits in a venture round
tests.body: We back companies that reach revenue without having to own the factory, the fleet or the grid asset.
tests.evidence: AmpereHour commissioned 360 MWh on a $5M round; IndiGrid financed the asset.

whyNow.label: The shock
whyNow.source: China's licensing of seven medium and heavy rare earths, in force since April 2025
whyNow.body: The controls have never been lifted. India's answer is a ₹7,280 crore magnet scheme.

whyNow.label: The buyer
whyNow.source: 75% of the defence capital budget reserved for domestic industry, February 2026
whyNow.body: One buyer, the defence ministry, funds satellites, quantum navigation, drone batteries and aerospace alloys.

whyNow.label: The proof
whyNow.source: QKD units delivered to the Indian Navy in 2024, two years after an iDEX challenge
whyNow.body: A startup won a government challenge, delivered the systems, and that same government now funds the company.

tests.notFund: Battery cells, green hydrogen at system scale, quantum computers, whole launch vehicles. When the first plant costs more than a venture round we back suppliers instead of the plant.
tests.changeView: China lifts its export controls. An Indian chip plant approves a domestic supplier. A space parts company raises at a seed-stage price.
